title.narrative: Advancing climate-smart conservation agriculture across Southern Tajikistan

description.narrative: 3 land scarce communities in Ishkashim district turn 68 ha of fallow land into models for resource conserving pomiculture. Welthungerhilfe is currently installing solar water pumps for irrigation. The project complements this measure by adding a component for resource conserving pomiculture, allowing beneficiaries to make maximum use of their precious new water and soil resources.The approach will be rolled out to protect soil and water in Southern Tajikistan's agricultural areas and improve food security and income opportunities of agricultural smallholders. Through the project's innovative approaches, over 100ha of currently unproductive lands are turned into extensive orchards, fodder or vegetable gardens that are managed according to the principles of conservation agriculture.

Climate smart irrigation, pomi- and horticulture contribute to the protection of soil and water in Southern Tajikistan's agricultural areas and improve food security and income opportunities of hundreds of agricultural smallholders. Through the projects innovative approaches, over 100ha of currently unproductive lands are turned into extensive orchards, fodder or vegetable gardens that are managed according to the principles of conservation agriculture.

The beneficiaries of this project are agricultural smallholders in the 6 target districts of Shugnon, Rushon, Ishkashim, Yovon, Khuroson and Vakhsh. In total, >800 dekhan farmer families will benefit from this intervention, resulting in >4000 people (family members) as indirect beneficiaries – among which 50% women. Approximately 400 families will be allocated land plots on the newly irrigated lands. The same amount of smallholders in neighboring villages will additionally participate in the trainings provided by the project. These people already have fruit trees in their home gardens and will learn how to properly tend them using the resource conserving practices, promoted by the project.While some target villages in the Ishkashim regions are already identified and confirmed by authorities and beneficiary communities, the final identification of additional land plots in the remainder of the target zone will happen during the first 4 months of the project (inception period). This selection is based on a list of potential project locations, which have already been pre assessed.
